paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : Caption not extracted
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy from 60% to 85%. Each method is represented by a distinct colored line with corresponding markers: Base (black, solid line, circle markers), MEND (brown, solid line, diamond markers), FT (blue, solid line, triangle markers), MEMIT (purple, solid line, pentagon markers), and ROME (green, solid line, square markers). As the co-occurrence number increases, all methods show an upward trend in accuracy. At the lowest co-occurrence number (1), the Base method starts at approximately 64%, MEND at 70%, FT at 65%, MEMIT at 69%, and ROME at 74%. At the highest co-occurrence number (1000), the Base method reaches about 71%, MEND reaches approximately 80%, FT reaches around 73%, MEMIT reaches about 77%, and ROME reaches the highest accuracy of approximately 84%. The ROME method consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, while the Base method consistently has the lowest accuracy.
